scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: A Campus 1 user on VLAN 10 (PC5, 172.16.10.x) reports they
cannot reach hosts on VLAN 30 (172.16.30.x) -- inter-VLAN routing on the Campus 1
multilayer switch seems broken. They suspect one of mswitch0's SVIs
(172.16.10.254 / 172.16.30.254) is down or misconfigured. Please confirm the SVI
fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Inter-VLAN routing on the Campus 1 multilayer switch (mswitch0) is healthy; no SVI fault is present. On mswitch0, both SVIs are up and correctly addressed: vlan10@br0 has 172.16.10.254/24 and vlan30@br0 has 172.16.30.254/24, both in state UP, LOWER_UP. The routing table confirms these are directly connected networks (172.16.10.0/24 via vlan10, 172.16.30.0/24 via vlan30). From an endpoint perspective, PC5 (172.16.10.5) can reach its default gateway 172.16.10.254 with 0% loss and has a valid ARP entry for it. Cross-VLAN connectivity is also working: the topology-wide reachability test shows PC5 successfully pinging a VLAN 30 host (pc13, 172.16.30.13) with no packet loss, and a VLAN 30 host (pc12) can reach its SVI 172.16.30.254 as well.

Mechanism: Because both SVIs are operational and installed as connected routes on mswitch0, traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 30 is routed locally on the switch. The observed successful pings corroborate correct L3 forwarding and ARP resolution on both sides.

Localization: No faulty interface or process on mswitch0; vlan10 and vlan30 SVIs are functioning. Endpoints PC5 and VLAN 30 hosts respond as expected.

Root cause: No misconfiguration or downed SVI found; the reported outage is not reproducible and was likely transient or endpoint-specific.

Corrective fix: None required on mswitch0. If issues persist for the user, verify the target host’s availability/firewall and the user PC’s local settings (IP/netmask/gateway) during the incident window.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states mswitch0 VLAN10/30 SVIs are up (UP, LOWER_UP), shows connected routes and successful cross-VLAN pings, confirming inter-VLAN routing is healthy at baseline.

Inferences that inter‑VLAN routing is healthy follow logically and the investigation covers the essential checks.
